Groundwater total dissolved solids, salinity, and fouling potential may vary spatially and would need to be characterized in detail for site-specific feasibility and system design. As the water is circulated through heat exchangers and returned to the subsurface without net water consumption, water costs do not factor into the capital or operational estimates. Instead, water savings associated with the avoided evaporative losses in conventional cooling towers were incorporated as revenue. 4.2.2 Capital Cost • Drilling: Drilling cost was estimated using an empirical correlation of $1 million for a 1- km-deep production well (Lowry et al. 2017) and $200/m for a 200-m-deep injection well (Oh et al. 2025b). The $1 million for the production well drilling represents ideal cost, while the shallow well cost may vary regionally. These estimates also exclude additional expenses such as directional drilling or mobilizing rigs to the island. Future study is recommended to address the uncertainties in drilling costs. Similar to the two chiller capital cost scenarios, this study considered two GeoSWAC configurations, single 29 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. doublet or two doublets, to address uncertainties in deep geologic conditions (e.g., in situ fracturing pressures, flow constraints). Total drilling costs were estimated at $1,040,000 for the one-doublet system and $2,080,000 for the two-doublet system. • Heat Exchangers: Capital cost of the heat exchangers required to meet the peak cooling load of 4.9 MW in Figure 14c was estimated at $391,902, using $140/GPM (Oh et al. 2025b) and the peak flow rate of 2,799.3 GPM (176.6 kg/s). • Piping: Surface piping between the well field and the central plant was assumed to span 500 m (250 m for each of supply and return lines). At a unit cost of $519.8/m (Oh et al. 2025b), the total piping cost was estimated at approximately $259,900. • Pumps: The peak system flow rate and associated pressure drops were used to estimate the peak pumping power. Using the pumping power and $1,000/kW (Oh et al. 2025b), the capital cost was estimated at $391,373 for the single-doublet system (391.4 kW) and $195,767 for the two-doublet system (195.8 kW).
